en: Now I shall describe the procedure for bathing as revealed by the Supreme Lord, by which one who has bathed attains perfection and is liberated from sin. 1.
Having bathed in rivers, streams, lakes, and excellent pools,
one should daily perform the ritual bath according to the general rules prescribed.
Therein, first, being pure, having sipped water for purification, and composed in a clean place,
one should take earth that has been purified with the Astra mantra, while reciting the Sadyojāta mantra.
Then, having placed it in a watery place, the knower of mantras should sprinkle it with the Vāmadeva mantra and consecrate it with this Bahurūpa mantra.
Then, having divided it into three parts, one should cast three parts with the steps of the Puruṣa-sūkta in the various directions, and one part, consecrated with the Astra-mantra, into the water.
One should cause half a portion to be used for cleansing the impurities in water, and place another half aside;
with one portion, however, one should perform the rite of Śivatīrtha by means of the elevenfold self.

Having first established Śiva in his upper body starting from the front with the mantras beginning with Īśāna and the others in sequence, he should afterwards bathe [the deity] with *āmalaka* and other substances.

Having performed the consecration and the breath-restraints (prāṇāyāma) with those very [mantras] by Śiva, and having sipped water (ācamana), the twice-born ascetic should first perform the Brāhmaṇical twilight devotion (saṃdhyā). 8.
But the other, whose nature is dispassion and who is turned away from worldly objects, should perform the Brāhmī initiation or, by rule, the Śaivī alone. || 9 ||
One should perform the cleansing with the Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, and then Aghora mantras;
one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) with the fourth [mantra], and apply the remainder with the Īśāna mantra.
Having withdrawn [the deity] by means of Śrīkaṇṭha, one should perform the rite for oneself within the heart;
then, having meditated upon the form that is eternally radiant, one should proceed to the sanctuary.
Another bath, known as the fiery bath (āgneyasnāna), is declared to be the ash-bath;
it may be performed daily after the water-bath, or even as a superior alternative to it.

The ash, which is unseen [by ordinary perception], has been proclaimed by those expert in the ritual bathing with ash as being the very essence of the performance of action that touches upon the intermingling of castes. 13.
White, pure, hairless, and indeed free from any attachment—
therefore, the fire-born bath (āgneya-snāna) is praised as superior in its qualities.
Facing north, one should bathe daily with pure forest cow-dung or with mineral earth, which has been consecrated with mantras such as "sadyojāta" and others.
One should successively dust the head, face, neck, shoulders, arms, and chest; finally, one should dust the hips.
Having sipped water three times, one should then gently wipe the mouth twice and subsequently touch the head and the six apertures of the head.
Then, having sprinkled water on the shoulders, the heart, the navel, and finally the head, as well as the two feet, one should perform here what has been prescribed.
At the base of the thumb, the Brāhma-tīrtha is established;
having sipped water from that, one is always pure when facing either the east or the north. (19)
The *daiva* tīrtha is praised as being at the base of the little finger;
by that [tīrtha], the wise praise the drinking of water itself. 20.
The supreme sacred site (tīrtha) for the libation of the sages is located at the tip of the finger;
for the rites pertaining to the ancestors, it is at the base of the thumb and forefinger.
The fire-element (āgneya) is located in the middle of the right hand, while the moon-element (saumya) is established in the left;
by means of these two positions, one should perform the consecration that destroys all sins.
There is another bath called Māhendra which is prescribed when rain has fallen;
for that which involves contact with the rays of the sun is indeed more highly esteemed.
With eyes closed like those of an elephant, facing eastward with arms raised,
one should recite the Īśāna mantra while taking seven steps.
And likewise, the Vāyavya bath should be performed with dust raised by cows, using the Tatpuruṣa mantra alone, by one who knows the procedure for bathing. (25)
One should know that sprinkling with water purified by the *sadyojāta* mantra and others is the "mantric" rite; this is also prescribed for the *vāruṇa* (water) rite. 26.

The mental [recitation] should be performed with the mind; it is the sixth [type], and it is universal. It is performed with the initial mantra of all mantras and by means of the breath-control (prāṇāyāma). || 27 ||
Having bathed and sipped water according to the rule, and having performed the ritual acts as prescribed,
one should then worship the Lord of Gods either in a linga, or on a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila),
or in the fire-pit, or in the body; this is proclaimed as the constant practice.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, on bathing, in the Svāyambhuva-sūtra-saṃgraha.
